**Scope.** Every video ad creative that a verified competitor ran on Meta (Ad Library, US view) or TikTok (Commercial Content Library, EU/UK/CH view) at any point in the rolling 30-day window ending 2026-09-12T20:28:49Z, analysed the way the organic slideshow research analysed videos: hook, beats, product reveal, claims, editing, footage sources, structure tag, and a mapping to the slideshow hook/format/principle taxonomy. No spend requirement was applied; nothing here is a performance claim, because neither library exposes impressions, spend or results for these ads.

**What was collected.** Meta: 56 competitor pages queried, 2385 in-window ad instances, 1805 with video, 2878 video renditions downloaded (0 failures), 1460 unique creatives after automatic dedup (1450 after inherited reviewer DEDUP NOTE merges on non-Fitbod T1). TikTok CCL: 83 keyword queries completed; advertiser-level enumerations for Nextgen Labs LLC (50/50 listed, end reached), SCRAMBLY SRL (406 listed of 5,147), GymBros inc / Liftoff (410 listed of 3,242), MyFitCoach GmbH (404 listed of 1,141), MyFitnessPal, Inc. (240/317 listed, end reached). Section 3 has the matrix; Section 7 lists every ad instance with its library URL and collection timestamp.

**What was analysed in full (written records).** 730 records in Section 4: every T1 Meta unique (628, including all 227 Fitbod) plus 102 TikTok uniques (Nextgen Labs 12 inherited; Liftoff 18, MyFitCoach 13, MyFitnessPal 15, Scrambly 44 newly written from downloaded slices). Meta Tier-2/3 (832 uniques across 30 advertisers) were collected, downloaded, frame-sampled, transcribed and clustered, but received no written record; they are quantified in Section 3 and scheduled in Section 9.

**Headline findings.**
- Mechanism competitors run small, fast-rotating sets (8–37 uniques each) built from a handful of structures: the caught-in-the-act skit → lock screen → exercise → scroll (S-A), the lock-screen mechanism explainer (S-B), the long skeptic-to-convert UGC testimonial with a Screen Time screenshot (S-C), and the static-caption confession (S-D).
- General-fitness advertisers run template families at volume. Fitbod's completed 227 uniques confirm the same production system as LazyFit: a small set of spines (creator muscle-group reels with a corner exercise-card inset; hypothetical week/month diaries; "I stopped X/Y/Z" confession → onboarding tour; interview cold-opens) behind many first-3-second variants and same-day re-launches.
- The only "same creative on two platforms" evidence in paid libraries remains AbMaxx / Nextgen Labs LLC (Section 5). Newly analysed TikTok slices for Liftoff, MyFitCoach, MyFitnessPal and Scrambly did not match Meta packs by perceptual/transcript identity in this recovery (they are separate platform cuts; presence on both libraries is not the same file).
- Advertising-library presence is not proof of performance. TikTok "Unique users seen" ranges are recorded as the platform field only.

**Where to look first.** Section 9.1 ranks reusable structures for a movement-gated screen-time app; Section 5 has the cross-advertiser structure index; Section 4 records are grouped by advertiser.

**Recovery contradictions (resolved from files, not from placeholders).** Placeholders said 459 records and Fitbod "227 unrecorded"; disk had 489 inherited CREATIVE IDs including 76 Fitbod. Placeholders said Scrambly 5 details and new advertisers "not enumerated"; disk had 63 Scrambly details and listing+slice files for Liftoff/MyFitCoach/MyFitnessPal captured 2026-09-12T19:25Z–20:28Z. s3_totals said Fitbod 46 records; five inherited Fitbod files actually held 76. `/tmp/fm-competitor-ad-video-30d` was empty. "86 creative packs" = 43 slug packs × `.md`+`.json`. "30 analysis files, >1,300 analyses" = 30 record markdowns and 2,344 `analysis.json` artifacts.

## 1. Window and methodology

**Rolling 30-day window (UTC).** Start `2026-08-13T15:41:44Z`; collection began `2026-09-12T15:41:44Z`; window end = last capture timestamp in this pass: `2026-09-12T20:28:49Z`. Every ad below carries the collection timestamp of the query that returned it (Section 7).

**Inclusion rules (verbatim from the brief, applied mechanically).**
- Meta Ad Library: an ad is in scope if it was active at any point in the window, i.e. `is_active == true` at capture time OR `delivery_stop_time >= 2026-08-13`. Meta exposes delivery dates at day granularity only (`YYYY-MM-DDT02:00:00`), so the test is on the date; ads whose start date is `2026-08-13` are flagged "boundary-day start". Ads whose start date is before `2026-08-13` are flagged "pre-window start" (they are in scope because they were still delivering inside the window).
- TikTok Commercial Content Library (CCL): an ad is in scope if its "Last shown" date is on/after `2026-08-13`; the library's own `start_time`/`end_time` filter (which operates on the last-shown date) was set to the window, and each ad's "First shown"/"Last shown" were re-read from the detail page.
- "Currently active" = Meta `is_active == true` at capture; "ended in window" = Meta ad with `is_active` not true and stop date inside the window. TikTok's CCL does not expose an active flag: an ad whose last-shown date is the capture day or the day before is reported as "last shown <date>" only.
- Excluded: namesake advertisers (verified via each candidate's registered identity, App Store publisher or the ad's destination link), political ads (the Move To Scroll page's two 2025 ZAR political ads are outside the window anyway), static-image ads (counted in the coverage matrix as "image-only" but not analysed), ads whose creative could not be fetched (counted as inaccessible, never described from guesses).

**Meta collection.** Page-level queries through the local `meta-ads-collector` CLI (`--page-url https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?view_all_page_id=<page_id> -c US -s all -n 400 --page-size 30 --sort-by relevancy`). Country filter `US`; status `all`. The CLI caps a page at 400 ads; pages that returned exactly 400 are flagged "cap 400 hit" in the coverage matrix because in-window ads beyond the cap may exist (Fitbod, The Conqueror Challenges, WeRise, and any T2/T3 page marked the same way). For every in-window ad the video creative(s) were downloaded immediately from the signed `video_hd_url` → `video_sd_url` → `video_url` (fbcdn URLs expire within hours, so they are recorded as "expiring; local copy" rather than as durable creative URLs). One ad can carry several placement renditions of the same creative (`__c0`, `__c1`, `__c2` = different aspect ratios); each is counted as a video instance and then collapsed by exact-byte (md5) and perceptual matching. Meta exposes `impressions`, `spend` and `reach` only for political/issue ads; for every ad here the fields are null and are reported as `not exposed`.

**TikTok CCL collection.** Headless Chrome driven by `chrome-devtools-axi` (no login, no cookie reuse). Two query types: keyword discovery (`query_type=1`, `adv_name=<competitor name>`, sorted by last-shown desc, first ~24 cards read per query) to find which competitor identities advertise there at all, and advertiser-level listing (`query_type=2&adv_biz_ids=<id>`, resolved from a verified ad's "See all ads" link) to enumerate every in-window ad of a verified advertiser. Each ad's detail page (`https://library.tiktok.com/ads/detail/?ad_id=<id>`) supplies: advertiser, "Ad paid for by", registered location, first/last shown, "Unique users seen" (a range, recorded verbatim under that field name), the country/age/gender reach table, the external website link, and the `<video>` source (a signed `library.tiktok.com/api/v1/cdn/...` URL, downloaded with the page's referer; not durable). The CCL only lists ads that were shown in the EU/EEA, UK or Switzerland; that is a hard regional limit of the source (Section 8). Mid-run the library answered HTTP 429 on its `api/v1` endpoints; collection was paused (no rate-limit circumvention), a probe was re-tried every 5 minutes, and the remaining queries were re-run at a paced rate (≥12 s between page loads, 90 s+ back-off on any empty page). Every query result that came back as an empty shell during the 429 episode was discarded and re-run, or listed as a gap if it could not be re-run.

**Video analysis.** For every downloaded video: `ffprobe` (duration, resolution, fps, audio presence), exact frames at 0/1/2/3 s (540 px), a frame every 2 s (every duration/30 s for videos over 60 s, max 30 frames), a mid and an end frame, two contact sheets (`sheet_first3s.jpg`, `sheet_seq.jpg`), a 16 kHz mono audio extraction, an English ASR transcript with `whisper.cpp` tiny.en (segment timestamps kept; ASR quotes are marked "(ASR)" because the tiny model mis-hears brand names), Tesseract OCR per frame (used only as a hint; on-screen text in the records was read from the frames), a 64-bit DCT perceptual hash of the full frame and of the centre-square crop for the 0/1/2/3 s, mid and end frames, and the mean audio level. Every record's hook, beats, product reveal, claims and editing fields were written by reading the two contact sheets plus the timed transcript for that creative (and single frames where needed).

**Deduplication.** Exact byte duplicates (md5) collapse first. Then, within an advertiser, two videos are the *same creative* if their durations differ by ≤0.6 s and at least 4 of the 6 sampled centre-crop hashes are within Hamming distance 12 (or 4 of 6 full-frame hashes within 10, or the ASR transcripts are ≥0.92 similar with ≥2 close hashes), or if durations differ by ≤0.2 s and the transcripts are ≥0.97 similar. Two creatives are *variants of one family* (same footage, different hook/length/CTA/aspect) if their transcripts are ≥0.6 similar, or both mid and end hashes are within 12, or ≥3 of the first-4 hashes are within 12; families are named `<slug>-Fxx` and the record for each variant states what changed. Cross-advertiser identity of a creative was checked with the same hash/transcript comparison across all packs. Every ad instance (ad ID + placement rendition) is retained in the source index even when collapsed.

**What the records are and are not.** Each record describes only what is visible in the frames, audible in the transcript, or stated in the ad's library metadata. "WHY IT MAY BE RUNNING" lists observable reuse/testing signals (instances, active/ended, date span, re-launch under new ad IDs, collation counts) and never treats presence, duration or count as performance evidence. TikTok "Unique users seen" ranges are reported exactly as shown; nothing else is a performance metric. Mapping to the slideshow hook/format/principle taxonomy uses the exact entry names from `research/slideshows/hooks.md`, `formats.md` and `principles-and-lessons.md`, with `no clean match` where none applies.

## 2. Coverage matrix

**Who was attempted.** Every competitor that the prior creative report (`competitor-creative-30d`, Section 3) confirmed as paid-active on a verified Meta page (48 pages), plus the verified mechanism-niche entrants and secondary pages it listed (Grindlock, Strut, Mogged ×2, Scrambly ×2, WalkUp ×2, AbMaxx, Rate My Physique, Muscle Monster, Muscle Booster, LazyFit, Fitbod, The Conqueror Challenges, WeRise), 56 Meta pages in total (`raw/adv30d/meta/targets.json`). Tiering: T1 = lock-until-you-move / screen-time-gating apps and the physique/discipline apps that sell the same "earn it" mechanic, plus the four highest-volume general-fitness advertisers the prior report flagged; T2 = walking-reward, habit and workout-planner apps; T3 = broad fitness/pilates brands. Pages that the prior report had already inspected and excluded as namesakes were **not** re-attempted and are not counted anywhere here: "Lockt" (wearlockt.com glasses), three "Stryde" pages (getstryde.co knee straps), "ScreenTime" (Dexerto media), two "Rivo" pages (fintech, musician), "The Steppers" (band), "John Anderson" (ReelShort drama), "Smash" (file transfer), "SHEFIT" (sports bras), two "Better Together" pages (political PAC / nonprofit), "Mettle" (mettlebyabby.com), "Strut" 441350676018663 (sexual-health clinic), "Liftoff" (Steam game), "A-Health" 1237943216062757 (other app IDs). Their in-window ads are namesake ads, not competitor ads.

**How to read the table.** "ads returned" = what the US library view returned for the page (cap 400; "cap 400 hit" means the page has at least 400 ads and in-window ads beyond the cap may exist). "in-window ads" = active at capture or stop date ≥ 2026-08-13. "video / image-only" splits in-window ads by whether the creative carries a video; image-only ads are counted but not analysed (out of scope). "active / ended" = library `is_active` at capture vs ended inside the window. "pre-window starts" = in-window ads whose delivery began before 2026-08-13. "video instances" = downloaded renditions (one ad can carry up to three placement renditions of one creative). "unique" = distinct creatives after md5 + perceptual/ASR dedup (Section 1). "0" rows with "ads returned 0" are pages the library returned empty for the US view (Grindlock, Strut 489495881077392, Mogged 836938016172845); Mogged alt page 1006749932526896 returned 3 ads, all ended before the window.

## 4. Creative records (one per accessible unique creative with a written record)

One record per accessible unique creative, grouped by advertiser in tier order (T1 = lock-until-you-move / mechanism-adjacent apps first). Field labels follow the brief. Everything in a record comes from the creative's frames (the 0/1/2/3 s frames and the 2 s sequence), its ASR transcript (quotes marked "(ASR)"; whisper tiny.en mis-hears brand names, obvious corrections are in brackets), on-screen text read from the frames, and the ad's library metadata. Inference is labelled as such. `not exposed` means the platform returns no value for that field. "WHY IT MAY BE RUNNING" lists only observable reuse/testing signals; nothing in this section is a performance claim. Local evidence for each creative lives under `raw/adv30d/analysis/<platform>/<slug>/<rep_key>/` in the worktree (contact sheets, frames, transcript, analysis.json) and the video under `raw/adv30d/<platform>/videos|ads/<slug>/`; these are scratch files, not deliverables.

### 4.1 Pushscroll: Exercise To Scroll (META, slug `pushscroll`)
#### pushscroll-U01 — 
- **CREATIVE ID:** pushscroll-U01 (family pushscroll-F05 with U35 — shared ending footage, end-frame hash distance 0, ASR similarity 0.61; U35 is in batch B)
- **COMPETITOR / ADVERTISER:** Pushscroll (Meta page 705689182637225)
- **PLATFORM / AD IDS:** Meta; 3 ad instances, byte-identical video: 1686975920095215 (collation 1609607274060046, collation_count 3), 1619805769858477, 1050899781161929
- **AD LINKS:** https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=1686975920095215 · https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=1619805769858477 · https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=1050899781161929 · file `raw/adv30d/meta/videos/pushscroll/1686975920095215__c0.mp4` · analysis `raw/adv30d/analysis/meta/pushscroll/1686975920095215__c0/`
- **DELIVERY WINDOW:** 1686975920095215: 2026-08-20→2026-08-28 (ended); 1619805769858477: 2026-08-30→2026-09-01 (ended); 1050899781161929: 2026-09-01→2026-09-02 (ended). All started in window; none active at collection. Pattern: the same file re-launched three times in 13 days.
- **DESTINATION / CTA:** App Store id6741765734; CTA "Install now". Body copy differs from the page default: "You wake up. Open Instagram. Open TikTok. Then suddenly your motivation for the day is gone. That's because your brain just got flooded with dopamine before you even got out of bed. Pushscroll blocks your favorite apps until you've earned them with movement. Instead of starting my mornings with reels, I start with pushups. It's one small change that's completely transformed my routine."
- **FIRST 3 SECONDS / HOOK:** Frames 0/1/2/3 s: living room, a guy in a light-blue tee does jumping jacks in front of a TV showing a football match, snacks and a soda on the table; a Snapchat-style black caption strip reads "Bro can't scroll unless he exercises 😭😭" on every frame. Spoken: friend off-camera "Dude, earn your screen time later, it's the World Cup" / "Nah man, I won't scroll now" (0–4.6 s). Spoken hook = social conflict (friend heckles him); on-screen hook = third-person "bro" meme caption. Curiosity mechanism: why is he exercising in the living room during the match? Emotional trigger: amusement plus recognition of the doomscroll habit.
- **FORMAT:** 42.7 s, 9:16, 720×1280, live-action UGC. Two-part: phone-shot "caught" clip (0–6 s) → first-person voice-over explainer with one-word white bold kinetic captions (UNLESS / CHEAT / TRACKS / SCREEN / SQUATS …) over b-roll and screen recordings → talking-head close (40–42 s) with app icon.
- **STORY / PROGRESSION:** Beats: (1) 0–6 s friend films him exercising instead of watching the match; (2) 6–9 s phone on floor, "TikTok blocked by Pushscroll" screen, "I can't scroll unless I exercise first. I can't cheat either"; (3) 9–19 s mechanism: in-app rep tracker with skeleton overlay and "Collect 2/41/50 Minutes" buttons, app home "51 min, Daily Goal 44/53, Push-ups, Steps, Squats"; (4) 19–27 s benefit: "instead of reels I'm starting my day with 50 push-ups… replacing [bad habits] is something that actually works" over Instagram feed → "Instagram blocked by Pushscroll"; (5) 27–34 s habit shift: journey mode, streak, jumping-jack timer "1/50 Level 232"; (6) 34–39 s transformation: river/lake landscape, handstand between two chairs, "days longer, head clearer, doing things I never thought I'd be physically capable of"; (7) 39–42 s CTA "replace your scrolling with something healthier, download Pushscroll", app icon. Audience: young men who scroll; story type: caught-in-the-act → convert explainer.
- **PRODUCT REVEAL:** Blocked-app screen at ~8 s, app UI (tracker, home, settings) from 10 s onward; name spoken at 42 s; icon at 42 s.
- **PROOF / CLAIMS:** Claims: exercise unlocks screen time, tracking prevents cheating, push-ups/[planks]/lunges/steps all earn minutes, "life-changing", 50 push-ups every morning, journey mode + streaks, clearer head. Proof shown: in-app counters and daily-goal screen only. No ratings, no numbers, no disclosures. Metrics: `not exposed`.
- **VISUALS / EDITING / AUDIO:** Phone footage, mixed indoor rooms, outdoor landscape inserts; cuts every ~2 s; one-word caps captions synced to VO; VO is the creator's own voice, casual; background music not distinguishable in the transcript (mean volume −16.7 dB). Text volume: low (one word per frame after the caption strip). Footage source: self-shot UGC plus screen recordings.
- **WHY IT MAY BE RUNNING:** (inference) The library shows the identical file launched three separate times (08-20, 08-30, 09-01) with a long dopamine-morning body copy, which suggests the advertiser kept re-entering it as a control while testing other hooks. All three instances had ended by collection. No performance evidence exposed.
- **WHAT TO STEAL:** The two-stage shape: a 5-second third-person "caught" clip with a meme caption, then a plain first-person mechanism explainer. The "I can't cheat either" line answering the obvious objection within 10 s. Ending on a physical-capability payoff (handstand) rather than a screen-time number.
- **WHAT NOT TO COPY:** The World Cup reference dates the ad. "Life-changing" and "actually works" are unsupported claims. The rapid room/location churn makes the middle feel like a montage rather than one person's story.
- **APP ANGLE MAP:** ExcerLock version: a friend heckles the user for exercising before opening an app ("just scroll, the game's on"), then the user explains the lock-until-you-move rule in first person; end on something they can now physically do. Requires only the block-until-exercise mechanic; swap the exercise list to whatever ExcerLock tracks.
- **REMIX DIFFICULTY:** Low — two people, one phone, one living room; the explainer is a screen-record plus VO.
- **PATTERN STATUS:** Within Pushscroll: the literal "Bro can't scroll unless/till he …" caption appears in U01 and U05, and the same third-person "bro/he" caption grammar in U07, U08, U09, U13; mechanism-explainer body repeated across U01, U05, U06, U10. Across advertisers: not checked in this batch.
- **MAPPING:** hooks.md → "Another person, conflict or doubt, then a changed reaction" (friend heckles, he refuses), "Repeatable signature" (the "Bro can't scroll" caption). formats.md → "Swap format" (replace reels with push-ups), "Content, warmup, product push". principles-and-lessons.md → "Blend into the feed" (Snapchat caption strip), "Sell the transformation, not the ingredient" (handstand ending), "Treat winners like a mining claim" (same file relaunched ×3).
- **STRUCTURE TAG:** `caught-bro-hook → mechanism-explainer`

## 5. Repeated-format index

Structures that recur are listed from most to least widely used. "Advertisers" counts distinct advertisers whose in-window video ads use the structure; "creatives" counts unique creatives (Section 4 IDs). A structure is marked **cross-advertiser** when ≥2 advertisers use it and **per-advertiser** when only one does. Nothing here is performance-validated: the platforms expose no impressions, spend, reach or results for any of these ads, so repetition is a reuse/testing signal only (the same caveat as the brief's "validated multi-account" rule in the prior organic report, which cannot be met with paid-library data). Structure letters (S-A …) are used in Section 9. Counts cover the tiers with completed records (see Section 3 for which advertisers that is).

| # | structure (abstract) | advertisers | creatives (Section 4 IDs) | scope | what varies between advertisers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-A | **Caught-in-the-act caption skit → lock/blocked screen → exercise or steps → reward scroll.** A third-person or POV caption strip in frame 1 ("Bro can't scroll till he does push-ups", "2AM craving → 20 squats", "my phone won't let me…"), a real person shown blocked, the exercise counted on screen, the feed unlocking. | 5 | Pushscroll U01, U04–U07, U09–U11, U13, U21, U23, U26, U28, U30, U33–U36; Workout Locker U01–U07, U09–U14, U17, U19, U20, U22–U24; Unrot U01, U03, U05, U10, U16, U24 (two-guys contrast); Move To Scroll U01, U07; DAWG U01, U04, U05, U07, U11, U13–U16 (reaction caption → tabletop scroll) | cross-advertiser | Pushscroll and Unrot use a witness/roommate who narrates; Workout Locker uses silent one-actor skits with music; DAWG drops the lock beat entirely (reaction → app scroll, no outro); Move To Scroll cuts to a native iOS screen recording. |

**Fitbod after recovery (227/227 records).** The completed set is a per-advertiser production system, not a new cross-advertiser structure. Recurring Fitbod spines: (1) creator muscle-group exercise lists with set×rep captions and a corner Fitbod exercise-card inset; (2) hypothetical week/month diaries ("if a [persona] used Fitbod for N weeks"); (3) "I stopped X / Y / Z" confession stacks into an onboarding/plan tour; (4) gym-interview cold-opens that convert the asker. Many pairs are placement renditions (4:5 vs 9:16) kept as separate uniques when the pack split them; records flag those as DEDUP NOTE / family links. Nothing in the Fitbod set is a performance claim.

**TikTok slices after recovery.** Liftoff (GymBros inc) 18 uniques, MyFitCoach 13, MyFitnessPal 15, Scrambly 44 — last-shown-desc samples, not full-library inventories. They did not add a new cross-advertiser structure that also appears in the completed Meta T1 set. Scrambly is walk-to-earn; treat it as adjacent-economy, not as a lock-until-you-move mechanic.

Repeated **devices** (smaller than a structure, seen across ≥3 advertisers): third-person Snapchat-style caption strip in frame 1 (Pushscroll, Workout Locker, Unrot, DAWG, Move To Scroll); the in-app rep counter with pose-skeleton overlay (Pushscroll, Workout Locker U17/U24); the "[App] blocked by …" shield/lock screen as the first product moment (Pushscroll, Workout Locker, Move To Scroll, Unrot); iOS Screen Time report screenshot as proof (Pushscroll, Unrot, Move To Scroll); word-by-word white-caps kinetic captions (Pushscroll, Rate My Physique, AbMaxx); music-only with one fixed caption (DAWG, Workout Locker, Unrot quiz, Move To Scroll); the same demo capture reused under different performers (DAWG "Level 63 / +29%" in five creatives; AbMaxx "89 overall / 11% body fat" card in ≥9; Move To Scroll "9,077 steps left" gate in two; Workout Locker night-kitchen squat footage in two).

Cross-advertiser identity check: no creative was found duplicated across two advertisers (147 mechanism-tier uniques compared by perceptual hash and transcript, 0 duplicates; one weak variant edge, Move To Scroll U08 ↔ Workout Locker U02, is a transcript-similarity coincidence between a text wall and a skit and was discarded).


**Same advertiser, two platforms (the only "multi-account" evidence available in paid libraries).** AbMaxx / Nextgen Labs LLC is the one advertiser in the completed tiers that is visible on both Meta (26 in-window ad instances, 19 uniques) and the TikTok CCL (50 in-window ad IDs, 12 uniques). Four structures run on both platforms (S-N, S-O, S-P, S-Q); the TikTok set adds a "symptom-reframe tutorial" (Nextgen Labs U01), a "false-belief gym skit → explainer" (U05), a "genre-tutorial bait → 'it's simpler than that' switch" (U07) and an "N reasons you can't X" diagnosis (U11) that have no Meta twin in the window. Scrambly (SCRAMBLY SRL) is also present on both libraries; its TikTok ads are enumerated in Section 2.3 and Section 8 states how far their analysis got.

## 7. Source index (2003 ad instances)

One row per ad ID (Meta) or ad ID (TikTok CCL). "Creative(s)" gives the unique-creative ID the ad's video was assigned to (Section 4) and, for Meta, the number of placement renditions downloaded for that ad. Delivery dates are the library's day-granular values (Meta) or the detail page's first/last-shown dates (TikTok). "Collected" is the UTC timestamp of the query that returned the row. Meta creative URLs are expiring signed fbcdn links and are therefore not reproduced; the durable pointer is the library URL plus the local file name `raw/adv30d/meta/videos/<slug>/<ad_id>__c<n>.mp4`. TikTok video URLs are likewise signed and expiring; the durable pointer is the detail URL.

## 8. Gaps

Every gap below is a hard limit of the source or of this pass; none is silently sampled. Counts are exact where the platform exposes them.

**8.1 Platform and region limits**
- **TikTok CCL covers only ads shown in the EU/EEA, UK and Switzerland.** US-only TikTok delivery is invisible; every Nextgen Labs and Scrambly country table read here lists the United Kingdom (and, for Scrambly, other EU countries where shown). A competitor with US-only TikTok campaigns will show "0 keyword hits" here even if it advertises heavily in the US. No workaround exists without platform access.
- **Meta Ad Library US view, no EU transparency rows.** Country/placement breakdowns, reach and audience tables are exposed only for ads delivered in the EU; for these US-view ads the library returns `publisher_platforms` only. Impressions, spend and reach are `not exposed` (null) for every non-political ad, which is all of them.
- **Meta delivery dates are day-granular** (`T02:00:00` on every value). Whether an ad that stopped on 2026-08-13 was still delivering after 15:41:44Z cannot be determined; such ads are flagged "boundary day" and included.
- **Meta `is_active` vs stop date disagree on some ads** (e.g. Pushscroll U11/U19/U25/U34, flagged in the records): the library's active flag was true while the stop date was the day before capture. Both values are reported; neither was overridden.
- **Meta creative URLs expire.** The signed fbcdn video URLs the library returns expire within hours; they are not reproduced. The durable pointer is the library ad URL; the analysed copy is the local file named in each record.
- **TikTok CCL exposes no active flag, no CTA text, no ad copy** (caption/body). "Last shown" is the only status signal; "Unique users seen" ranges and the country/age/gender tables are the only metrics, reported verbatim.

**8.2 Rate limits and interruptions**
- **TikTok CCL HTTP 429 at 16:10–16:32Z.** After ~90 page loads the library's `api/v1` endpoints returned 429 for both browser sessions. Collection was stopped, a probe was retried every 5 minutes, and the library answered again at 16:32:09Z; the remaining work then ran at ≥12 s between page loads with 90 s+ back-off on any empty page. Keyword results captured during the episode (WalkingPad+, WinWalk, Scrambly, WalkUp, Hot Girl Walk, Jaunt) were discarded and re-run. Two Nextgen Labs detail pages (1874433886070578, 1874433901673985) loaded as empty shells during the episode; they were re-fetched afterwards (result in Section 2.3). No rate-limit circumvention (session rotation, proxying, cookie reuse) was used.
- **Meta collector cap of 400 ads per page.** 8 pages returned exactly 400 ads; for those pages in-window ads beyond the cap may exist. Because the collector sorts by relevancy rather than date, the missing ads are not guaranteed to be older ones. Affected pages: Fitbod: Gym & Fitness Planner (1680675265485923), The Conqueror Challenges (608650595820049), WeRise App (299935279858942), Muscle Monster Workout Planner (363293240209119), Muscle Booster Workout Tracker (106059717857087), WalkUp | Weight Loss Tracker (709409825582498), Fabulous: Daily Habit Tracker (290983137688447), MyFitCoach - Workout Planner (108998620687821).

**8.3 Inaccessible creatives (counted, not described)**
- Meta: 580 in-window ads carry no video (image or carousel creatives); they are counted in Section 2.1 as "image-only" and excluded by the brief. 0 video downloads failed.
- TikTok CCL: 2 competitor detail pages exposed no `<video>` element (Nextgen Labs 1874433886070578/1874433901673985 were re-fetched in the original pass; MyFitnessPal 1876032357601602 in the recovery slice). They are counted, not described.
- Meta pages that returned no in-window ads: Grindlock (0 ads), Strut 489495881077392 (0 ads), Mogged 836938016172845 (0 ads), Mogged alt 1006749932526896 (3 ads, all ended before the window), and the T2/T3 pages listed with "0" in Section 2.1. "0 ads returned" is what the US library view returned for that page id at the capture time; it is not proof that the page has never advertised.

**8.4 Identity and attribution gaps**
- Rate My Physique: the prior report's Apple id 6746725862 does not resolve; every ad links id6739761800 (Rate My Physique: Body Scans, MagFit Inc.). Corrected in `targets.json` and in the records.
- TikTok keyword discovery surfaced advertiser identities that could not be attributed to a competitor without a verified link and are excluded: APPLABS LIMITED (ads for an AI-calorie app, not Rate My Physique), Scroll Vista (charger shop), Aggressive Workout (Lebanon, no link), TAYLOR & FRANCIS GROUP (Unrot keyword), META GAME LTD / The Financial Farmer / VOODOO (Conqueror keyword), official.stlshoty (DAWG), nnoxtinct / tuggeman / vibezsotuff (Mogged), JOE & THE JUICE / PURE GYM (Strut), Airforce BV / Concept padel / BAZOOKA (Move To Scroll), plus every name-only match in Section 2.2. Recovery did not promote Octopass or BePresent into the competitor set; they remain adjacent screen-time apps.
- Move To Scroll's page id 109435468131570 previously carried two May-2025 ZAR political ads for an unrelated permit site (page reuse); they are outside the window and were not counted.
- AbMaxx U01/U03 and Nextgen Labs U12 present themselves as CBS / Fox Business news segments; whether the footage is a real broadcast cannot be determined from frames and is not asserted.

**8.5 Extraction and analysis limits**
- ASR is whisper.cpp tiny.en: brand names are mis-heard in nearly every creative (e.g. "World Cuff" for Workout Locker, "AppMax" for AbMaxx); quotes are marked (ASR) and corrected only where the frame makes the word unambiguous. Two creatives have largely unintelligible audio (AbMaxx U18, U07's stitched clip).
- OCR (Tesseract) was used only as a hint; on-screen text in the records was read from the frames. Frames are sampled at 0/1/2/3 s and every 2 s (every duration/30 s above 60 s), so text or a beat that lasts under 2 s can be missed; three records note an end card that fell between samples (Rate My Physique U05) or a black/blank first frame (Pushscroll U13, U19).
- Perceptual clustering missed a few identical or edit-variant pairs that the reviewers caught by eye (AbMaxx U03 ≡ U11; Rate My Physique U10 ↔ U11; Pushscroll U04 ↔ U07, U09 ↔ U11; Nextgen Labs U04/U08/U10 and U06/U07/U11 script families). They are flagged in the records and corrected in the totals (Section 3); the automatic unique counts in Section 2.1 are the pre-correction values.
- Footage-source judgements (stock vs produced vs creator, AI-looking anime, same actress/set) are inferences from contact sheets and are labelled as such in the records.

**8.6 Scope not completed after this recovery (exact counts in Section 3 and Section 9)**
- Meta T2/T3: 832 unique creatives across 30 advertisers have packs/frames/ASR but no Section 4 records.
- TikTok listed-but-unfetched: Liftoff 390, MyFitCoach 384, MyFitnessPal 220, Scrambly 343 detail pages.
- TikTok unlisted remainder: Liftoff 3,242−410; MyFitCoach 1,141−404; Scrambly 5,147−406.
- Adjacent screen-time (Octopass, BePresent, Nibble, Deepstash) not in the competitor set.
- US-only TikTok delivery is invisible in the CCL.
- `/tmp/fm-competitor-ad-video-30d` contained no usable research files at recovery start.

## 9. Prioritised reusable structures and continuation plan

### 9.1 Prioritised reusable structures (relevance to a movement-gated screen-time app, then repeated use)

Nothing below is a performance ranking. Neither library exposes impressions, spend, or results for these ads. Order is: (1) structures that already sell a lock-until-you-move mechanic, (2) structures repeated across advertisers, (3) high-volume production systems that can carry a different product.

1. **S-A Caught-in-the-act caption skit → lock screen → exercise → reward scroll** — the closest native transfer. Used by Pushscroll, Workout Locker, Unrot, Move To Scroll, and (without the lock beat) DAWG. Steal the 5-second witness caption and the blocked-app proof; do not copy wording, characters, or footage.
2. **S-B Mechanism explainer with app capture** — lock → counter → minutes/steps → unlock. Four mechanism advertisers. The ExcerLock version is a screen recording of the gate, not a gym planner tour.
3. **S-C Long skeptic-to-convert UGC with a Screen Time screenshot** — four advertisers. The proof object is the iOS Screen Time report or a pickup count, not a physique.
4. **S-E Incumbent-vs-app contrast** ("Screen Time has an ignore button") — four advertisers. Transfer as "the built-in tool has a skip; this one does not."
5. **Fitbod / LazyFit production system (completed this recovery)** — fixed spine, hook-only variation, same-day re-launch under new ad IDs. Fitbod's 227 uniques are mostly: (a) creator muscle-group reels with a corner exercise-card inset, (b) hypothetical week/month diaries, (c) "I stopped X / Y / Z" confession stacks into an onboarding tour, (d) interview cold-opens. The reusable lesson is the system, not any gym claim.
6. **S-J Duration tests of one cold open** and **S-L store-twin / re-launch under new IDs** — ops patterns, not hooks.
7. **S-N…S-Q AbMaxx / Nextgen Labs cross-platform set** — the only same-creative-on-two-platforms evidence. Physique-niche; steal sequencing, not claims or footage.

Do not copy distinctive jokes, wordmarks, presenters, 15-million-user claims, or any before/after physique.
